title: ASR-complete
summary:
ASR-complete is, by analogy to NP-completeness in complexity theory, a term used to indicate that the difficulty of a computational problem is equivalent to solving the central automatic speech recognition problem, that is, recognizing and understanding spoken language.

The term follows a similar naming convention to other "-complete" problem classifications in computer science (like AI-complete), where solving any single ASR-complete problem would essentially require solving the full automatic speech recognition problem. This concept highlights that certain tasks in speech processing are fundamentally as hard as the general problem of understanding human speech.

Speech recognition, also known as automatic speech recognition (ASR), computer speech recognition, or speech-to-text (STT), is a sub-field of computational linguistics concerned with methods and technologies that translate spoken language into text or other interpretable forms. The ASR-complete designation indicates that some problems in this domain cannot be solved without essentially achieving full human-level speech understanding capability.
